draft.text: You came in because you have been having right knee pain, especially when swimming breaststroke.
The pain is a dull ache that gets sharper when moving your knee in certain ways.
You have not had swelling, stiffness, or instability in your knee.
The pain started after you increased your swimming frequency and intensity.
It has not improved with rest, and you have not tried any specific exercises for it yet.
The doctor suggested straight leg raises to strengthen your quadriceps.
You are waiting for the results of an MRI of your right knee to help confirm the cause of your pain.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have been having right knee pain, especially when swimming breaststroke, for a few weeks.
We found that you have no swelling, stiffness, or instability in your knee.
You also have no weakness in your quadriceps or trouble with straight leg raises.
Your doctor thinks you may have patellofemoral pain syndrome, which is pain around the kneecap, likely from overuse while swimming.
You are waiting for the results of an MRI of your right knee to confirm the diagnosis.
Your doctor suggested straight leg raises to strengthen your quadriceps.
